name: Lélia Gonzalez
shortBio: Afro-Brazilian philosopher, psychoanalyst, and Black feminist sociologist who forged Amefricanidade and Pretuguês, synthesizing Fanon and Lacan to dismantle Brazil's myth of "racial democracy."
centralQuestion: How does the ideology of "racial democracy" mask structural anti-Blackness in the Americas, and how does Amefricanidade center Afro-Indigenous agency?

keyWorks.title: Racism and Sexism in Brazilian Culture (Racismo e sexismo na cultura brasileira)
keyWorks.description: Psychoanalytic-sociological critique diagnosing Brazil's "cultural neurosis" of disavowing Black and female foundational subjectivity.

keyWorks.title: The Political-Cultural Category of Amefricanidade
keyWorks.description: Proposes Amefricanidade as a transnational epistemic horizon unifying Black and Indigenous resistance across the Americas.
